UỶ BAN THƯỜNG VỤ QUỐC HỘI                       CỘNG HOÀ XÃ HỘI CHỦ NGHĨA VIỆT NAM
                  ********                                     Độc lập - Tự do - Hạnh phúc
                                                                         ********

                Số: 09/1998/PL-UBTVQH10                                     Hà Nội, ngày 25 tháng 12 năm 1998

                                                   PHÁP LỆNH

   CỦA UỶ BAN THƯỜNG VỤ QUỐC HỘI SỐ 09/1998/PL-UBTVQH10 NGÀY 25 THÁNG 12 NĂM 1998 VỀ
                       TỔ CHỨC VÀ HOẠT ĐỘNG HOÀ GIẢI Ở CƠ SỞ

  Để phát huy truyền thống đoàn kết, tương thân, tương ái trong cộng đồng dân cư, nâng cao kết quả giải quyết
  những việc vi phạm pháp luật và tranh chấp nhỏ trong nhân dân ở cơ sở, góp phần phòng ngừa và hạn chế các
  vi phạm pháp luật, giữ gìn trật tự, an toàn xã hội, giảm bớt các vụ, việc phải xét xử tại Toà án;
  Căn cứ vào Hiến pháp nước Cộng hoà xã hội chủ nghĩa Việt Nam năm 1992;
  Căn cứ vào Nghị quyết của Quốc hội khoá X, kỳ họp thứ hai về Chương trình xây dựng luật, pháp lệnh năm
  1998;
  Pháp lệnh này quy định về tổ chức và hoạt động hoà giải ở cơ sở.

  Chương 1:

                                             NHỮNG QUY ĐỊNH CHUNG

  Điều 1. Hoà giải

  Hoà giải ở cơ sở là việc hướng dẫn, giúp đỡ, thuyết phục các bên đạt được thoả thuận, tự nguyện giải quyết với
  nhau những việc vi phạm pháp luật và tranh chấp nhỏ nhằm giữ gìn đoàn kết trong nội bộ nhân dân, phòng ngừa,
  hạn chế vi phạm pháp luật, bảo đảm trật tự, an toàn xã hội trong cộng đồng dân cư.

  Điều 2. Hình thức hoà giải

  Hoà giải ở cơ sở được thực hiện thông qua hoạt động của Tổ hoà giải hoặc các tổ chức thích hợp khác của nhân
  dân ở thôn, xóm, bản, ấp, tổ dân phố và các cụm dân cư khác phù hợp với pháp luật, đạo đức xã hội và phong
  tục, tập quán tốt đẹp của nhân dân.

  Nhà nước tạo điều kiện và khuyến khích hoạt động hoà giải, các hình thức hoà giải ở cộng đồng dân cư.

  Điều 3. Phạm vi hoà giải

  1- Việc hoà giải được tiến hành đối với những việc vi phạm pháp luật và tranh chấp nhỏ trong cộng đồng dân cư,
  bao gồm:

  a) Mâu thuẫn, xích mích giữa các cá nhân với nhau;

  b) Tranh chấp về quyền, lợi ích phát sinh từ quan hệ dân sự, hôn nhân và gia đình;

  c) Những việc vi phạm pháp luật khác mà theo quy định của pháp luật chưa đến mức bị xử lý bằng biện pháp
  hình sự hoặc biện pháp hành chính.

  2- Các vụ, việc sau đây không hoà giải :

  a) Tội phạm hình sự, trừ trường hợp mà người bị hại không yêu cầu xử lý về hình sự và không bị cơ quan nhà
  nước có thẩm quyền xử lý hành chính theo quy định của pháp luật;

  b) Hành vi vi phạm pháp luật bị xử lý hành chính;

  c) Vi phạm pháp luật và các tranh chấp mà theo quy định của pháp luật thì không được hoà giải.

  3- Nghiêm cấm mọi hành vi lợi dụng việc hoà giải để trốn tránh xử lý bằng biện pháp hình sự, hành chính.

  Điều 4. Nguyên tắc hoà giải

  Việc hoà giải được tiến hành theo các nguyên tắc sau đây:

  1- Phù hợp với đường lối, chính sách của Đảng, pháp luật của Nhà nước, đạo đức xã hội và phong tục, tập quán
  tốt đẹp của nhân dân;

  2- Tôn trọng sự tự nguyện của các bên; không bắt buộc, áp đặt các bên tranh chấp phải tiến hành hoà giải;

  3- Khách quan, công minh, có lý, có tình; giữ bí mật thông tin đời tư của các bên tranh chấp; tôn trọng quyền, lợi
  ích hợp pháp của người khác; không xâm phạm lợi ích của Nhà nước, lợi ích công cộng;

  4- Kịp thời, chủ động, kiên trì nhằm ngăn chặn vi phạm pháp luật, hạn chế những hậu quả xấu khác có thể xảy ra
  và đạt được kết quả hoà giải.

  Điều 5. Vai trò của Uỷ ban Mặt trận Tổ quốc Việt Nam, các tổ chức thành viên của Mặt trận, các tổ chức
  xã hội khác, tổ chức kinh tế, cơ quan nhà nước, đơn vị vũ trang nhân dân và công dân trong công tác hoà
  giải

  Uỷ ban Mặt trận Tổ quốc Việt Nam, các tổ chức thành viên của Mặt trận, các tổ chức xã hội khác, tổ chức kinh
  tế, cơ quan nhà nước, đơn vị vũ trang nhân dân và công dân có trách nhiệm phối hợp chặt chẽ với các cơ quan
  nhà nước hữu quan, động viên nhân dân trong việc xây dựng, củng cố Tổ hoà giải và các tổ chức hoà giải khác
  của nhân dân trong cộng đồng dân cư; giúp đỡ, tạo điều kiện cho hoạt động hoà giải ở cơ sở; tham gia hoà giải
  theo quy định của pháp luật.

  Điều 6. Quản lý nhà nước về công tác hoà giải

  1- Nội dung quản lý nhà nước về công tác hoà giải bao gồm:

  a) Ban hành văn bản pháp luật về tổ chức và hoạt động hoà giải;

  b) Hướng dẫn về tổ chức và hoạt động hoà giải;

  c) Tổ chức bồi dưỡng đường lối, chính sách của Đảng, pháp luật của Nhà nước, nâng cao nghiệp vụ hoà giải cho
  người làm công tác hoà giải;

  d) Sơ kết, tổng kết công tác hoà giải.

  2- Chính phủ thống nhất quản lý nhà nước về công tác hoà giải trong phạm vi cả nước.

  Bộ Tư pháp chịu trách nhiệm trước Chính phủ thực hiện quản lý nhà nước về công tác hoà giải ở cơ sở; chỉ đạo
  và hướng dẫn Uỷ ban nhân dân các cấp thực hiện quản lý nhà nước về công tác hoà giải ở địa phương.

  Chương 2:

                                   TỔ HOÀ GIẢI VÀ TỔ VIÊN TỔ HOÀ GIẢI

  Điều 7. Tổ hoà giải

  1- Tổ hoà giải ở cơ sở là tổ chức tự quản của nhân dân được thành lập ở thôn, xóm, bản, ấp, tổ dân phố và các
  cụm dân cư khác để thực hiện hoặc tổ chức thực hiện việc hoà giải những việc vi phạm pháp luật và tranh chấp
  nhỏ trong nhân dân theo quy định của pháp luật.

  2- Tổ hoà giải có tổ trưởng và các tổ viên do Uỷ ban Mặt trận Tổ quốc xã, phường, thị trấn phối hợp với các tổ
  chức thành viên của Mặt trận lựa chọn, giới thiệu để nhân dân bầu và do Uỷ ban nhân dân cùng cấp công nhận.

  Chính phủ quy định chi tiết thủ tục bầu, miễn nhiệm tổ trưởng và tổ viên Tổ hoà giải.

  Điều 8. Tổ trưởng Tổ hoà giải

  1- Tổ trưởng Tổ hoà giải là người phụ trách Tổ hoà giải, đồng thời tham gia hoạt động hoà giải với tư cách tổ
  viên.

  2- Tổ trưởng Tổ hoà giải có các nhiệm vụ sau đây:

  a) Phân công, điều hoà, phối hợp hoạt động của các tổ viên Tổ hoà giải; phối hợp hoạt động với Tổ hoà giải khác
  khi xét thấy cần thiết;

  b) Tổ chức rút kinh nghiệm về công tác hoà giải;

  c) Báo cáo Uỷ ban nhân dân, Uỷ ban Mặt trận Tổ quốc xã, phường, thị trấn về công tác hoà giải.

  Điều 9. Tiêu chuẩn của tổ viên Tổ hoà giải

  Tổ viên Tổ hoà giải có các tiêu chuẩn sau đây:

  1- Có phẩm chất đạo đức tốt, nghiêm chỉnh chấp hành chủ trương, chính sách của Đảng, pháp luật của Nhà nước
  và có uy tín trong nhân dân;

  2- Có khả năng thuyết phục, vận động nhân dân thực hiện chính sách, pháp luật;

  3- Tự nguyện tham gia tổ chức hoà giải, có tinh thần trách nhiệm, nhiệt tình trong công tác hoà giải.

  Chương 3:

                                             HOẠT ĐỘNG HOÀ GIẢI

  Điều 10. Tiến hành việc hoà giải

  Việc hoà giải được tiến hành trong các trường hợp sau đây:

  1- Tổ viên Tổ hoà giải chủ động hoà giải hoặc tổ chức việc hoà giải theo sáng kiến của mình;

  2- Theo sáng kiến của tổ trưởng Tổ hoà giải;

  3- Theo đề nghị của cơ quan, tổ chức hoặc cá nhân khác;

  4- Theo yêu cầu của một bên hoặc các bên tranh chấp.

  Điều 11. Người tiến hành hoà giải

  Việc hoà giải có thể do một hoặc một số tổ viên Tổ hoà giải tiến hành. Trong trường hợp cần thiết, tổ viên Tổ
  hoà giải có thể mời người ngoài Tổ hoà giải cùng tham gia hoà giải.

  Điều 12. Hoà giải tranh chấp mà các đương sự ở các cụm dân cư khác nhau

  Trong trường hợp các bên tranh chấp ở các cụm dân cư có các Tổ hoà giải khác nhau, thì các Tổ hoà giải đó phối
  hợp để thực hiện việc hoà giải.

  Điều 13. Phương thức hoà giải

  Việc hoà giải được tiến hành theo phương thức sau đây:

  1- Bằng lời nói;

  2- Trong trường hợp các bên có yêu cầu hoặc được các bên đồng ý, việc hoà giải được tổ viên Tổ hoà giải lập
  biên bản;

  3- Tuỳ từng trường hợp cụ thể, tổ viên Tổ hoà giải có thể tiến hành việc hoà giải bằng cách gặp gỡ từng bên hoặc
  các bên;

  4- Sau khi tìm hiểu sự việc, nguyên nhân phát sinh mâu thuẫn, tham khảo ý kiến của cá nhân, cơ quan, tổ chức
  hữu quan, lắng nghe ý kiến của các bên, tổ viên Tổ hoà giải phân tích, thuyết phục các bên đạt được thoả thuận
  phù hợp với pháp luật, đạo đức xã hội và phong tục, tập quán tốt đẹp của nhân dân và tự nguyện thực hiện thoả
  thuận đó.

  Điều 14. Kết thúc việc hoà giải

  Việc hoà giải được kết thúc khi các bên đã đạt được thoả thuận và tự nguyện thực hiện thoả thuận đó.

  Tổ viên Tổ hoà giải động viên, thuyết phục các bên thực hiện thoả thuận.

  Chương 4:

                                     KHEN THƯỞNG VÀ XỬ LÝ VI PHẠM

  Điều 15. Khen thưởng

  1- Tổ hoà giải và tổ viên Tổ hoà giải có thành tích trong công tác hoà giải thì được khen thưởng.

  2- Tổ chức, cá nhân có thành tích trong việc xây dựng, củng cố tổ chức và nâng cao hiệu quả hoạt động của các
  tổ chức hoà giải ở cơ sở, tích cực tham gia hoà giải thì được khen thưởng.

  Điều 16. Xử lý vi phạm

  Người nào có hành vi vi phạm Pháp lệnh này và các quy định khác của pháp luật về hoà giải ở cơ sở, thì tuỳ theo
  tính chất, mức độ vi phạm mà bị xử lý kỷ luật, xử phạt hành chính hoặc bị truy cứu trách nhiệm hình sự; nếu gây
  thiệt hại thì phải bồi thường theo quy định của pháp luật.

  CHƯƠNG V

                                            ĐIỀU KHOẢN THI HÀNH

  Điều 17. Phạm vi áp dụng

  1- Pháp lệnh này áp dụng đối với việc tổ chức và hoạt động của Tổ hoà giải ở cơ sở.

  Đối với những Tổ hoà giải ở cơ sở đã được thành lập trước ngày Pháp lệnh này có hiệu lực thì căn cứ vào các
  quy định của Pháp lệnh này để kiện toàn tổ chức và phát huy vai trò trong hoạt động hoà giải.

  2- Các quy định của Pháp lệnh này được áp dụng đối với hoạt động hoà giải của các tổ chức thích hợp khác của
  nhân dân trong cộng đồng dân cư ở cơ sở.

  Điều 18. Hiệu lực thi hành

  Pháp lệnh này có hiệu lực kể từ ngày công bố.

  Những quy định trước đây trái với Pháp lệnh này đều bãi bỏ.

  Điều 19. Hướng dẫn thi hành Pháp lệnh

  Chính phủ phối hợp với Uỷ ban Trung ương Mặt trận Tổ quốc Việt Nam hướng dẫn thi hành Pháp lệnh này.

                                                                    Nông Đức Mạnh

                                                                          (Đã ký)

1. Amendment to Article 10:

“Article 10. Competence to request for Vietnamese judicial entrustment

The authorities with competent to request for Vietnamese judicial entrustment consist of the
Supreme People’s Court; provincial People’s Courts; regional People’s Courts; civil judgment
enforcement agencies of provinces/cities; the Supreme People's Procuracy; provincial People’s
Procuracies; regional People’s Procuracies and other competent agencies in accordance with
regulations of law.”

“Article 17. Competence to execute foreign judicial entrustment

a) Regional People’s Courts;

entrustment relate to civil judgment enforcement;

During the process of executing foreign judicial entrustment, any of regional People’s Courts,
civil judgment enforcement agencies of provinces/cities may request any of agencies,
organizations, and individuals to give evidence or information in accordance with laws on civil
procedures and civil judgment enforcement.”

Affairs and the Chief Justice of the Supreme People's Court on procedures for judicial
assistance in civil matters

 ASSEMBLY OF VIETNAM                           Independence – Freedom – Happiness

     No: 106/VBHN-VPQH                                                     Hanoi, August 27, 2025

                                               LAW

                                   ON LEGAL ASSISTANCE

Pursuant to Law on Legal assistance No. 08/2007/QH12 dated November 21, 2007 of the
National Assembly of Vietnam, which has been effective since July 01, 2008 and is amended by:

Law No. 81/2025/QH15 dated June 24, 2025 of the National Assembly of Vietnam on
amendments to Law on Organization of People’s Courts dated July 01, 2025;

Pursuant to the Constitution of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam amended by the Resolution No.
51/2001/QH10;

The National Assembly promulgates the Law on Legal assistance.

Chapter I

                                   GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1. Scope

This Law provides principles, competence, and procedures for the provision of legal assistance
in civil and criminal cases, extradition and transfer of persons who are serving imprisonment
sentences between Vietnam and foreign countries; and responsibilities of Vietnamese regulatory
agencies in legal assistance.

Article 2. Regulated entities

This Law applies to Vietnamese agencies, organizations and individuals and foreign agencies,
organizations and individuals engaged in legal assistance activities with Vietnam.

Article 3. Application of law

1. Legal assistance complies with the provisions of this Law; in cases where this Law does not
provide, laws on civil procedures, laws on criminal procedures, and other relevant provisions of
Vietnamese laws shall apply.

2. Foreign laws are only applicable according to the provisions of international treaties of which
Vietnam is a member.

Article 4. Legal assistance principles

1. Legal assistance shall be provided in deference to national independence, sovereignty,
territorial integrity, non-intervention, equality and reciprocity in conformity to the Constitution
and laws of Vietnam and international treaties of which Vietnam is a member.

2. If Vietnam does not sign or accede to a relevant international treaty on legal assistance, the
legal assistance provision shall adhere to the principle of reciprocity and the laws of Vietnam,
international laws and practices.

Article 5. Language in legal assistance

1. In the case where there is a treaty on legal assistance between Vietnam and a foreign country,
the language in legal assistance is the language prescribed in that treaty.

2. In the case where there has been no treaty on legal assistance between Vietnam and a foreign
country, the application must enclosed with a translation in the language of the country requested
to provide legal assistance or a translation in another language accepted by the requested
country.

3. When an agency preparing a written request for legal assistance provision, the agency shall
translate it into the language prescribed in Clause 1 or Clause 2 of this Article.

Article 6. Legal mandate and form of provision of legal assistance

1. Legal mandate means a written request from the competent authority of Vietnam or foreign
competent authority regarding the implementation of one or a number of legal assistance
activities under the stipulated by the laws of the relevant country or international treaties of
which Vietnam is a member.

2. Legal assistance shall be provided on the basis of the request of a competent authority of
Vietnam or foreign competent authority via a legal mandate.

Article 7. Consular legalization and recognition of legal mandate documents

1. Consular legalization is the process by which the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, diplomatic
missions, consulates or other foreign agencies are authorized to perform the consular functions
of the signatures and seals on documents, issued, granted, or certified by the competent authority
of the foreign country for use in Vietnam.

2. Documents on legal assistance issued or certified by foreign competent authorities in
accordance with laws of the foreign country shall be recognized by the competent authority of
Vietnam if those documents have been consularly legalized.

Article 8. Summon and protection of witnesses and experts

1. During the proceedings, presiding authorities shall summon witnesses and experts under the
provisions of this Law and international treaties of which Vietnam is a member.

2. A summons must clearly state the conditions for the witness or expert and the commitment to
guarantee the life and health safety, accommodation, meal and travel conditions for the witness
or expert.

3. Witnesses and experts are given favorable entry and exit conditions under the provisions of
Vietnamese law.

4. Witnesses and experts summoned to Vietnam may not be arrested, detained, held in custody or
investigated, prosecuted or tried for the following acts before their arrival in Vietnam:

a) Providing testimonies or written expert conclusions on the cases for which they are
summoned;

b) Committing crime in Vietnam;

c) Having a relationship with the subject under investigation, prosecution, or trial in criminal
matters in Vietnam;

d) Being involved in other civil or administrative cases in Vietnam.

5. The right not to be arrested, detained, held in custody, or investigated, prosecuted, or tried of
witnesses, experts specified in Clause 4 of this Article shall cease if they do not leave Vietnam
within fifteen days after receiving written notices on their unnecessary presence in Vietnam from
the competent authorities of Vietnam. This period does not include the time when the witnesses,
experts cannot leave Vietnam due to force majeure.

Article 9. Transfer and receipt of documents, objects, and money

The transfer and receipt of documents, objects, and money for legal assistance activities must
comply with Vietnamese laws.

Chapter II

                                  CIVIL LEGAL ASSISTANCE

Article 10. Scope of civil legal assistance

The scope of civil legal assistance between Vietnam and foreign countries covers:

1. Service of documents related to civil legal assistance;

2. Summon of witnesses and experts;

3. Collection and provision of evidence;

4. Other requests for civil legal assistance.

Article 11. Requests for mutual legal assistance in civil matters

1. A request for mutual legal assistance in civil matters includes:

a) Request form for civil legal assistance of the competent authority;

b) Request form for mutual legal assistance in civil matters specified in Article 12 of this Law;

c) Other papers as requested by a competent body of the mandating country.

2. A request for mutual legal assistance in civil matters must be prepared in 03 sets in accordance
with this Law and in compliance with the laws of the mandating country. The language used in
the request must comply with Article 5 of this Law.

Article 12. Form to request for mutual legal assistance in civil matters

Request form for mutual legal assistance in civil matters includes:

1. Date, month, year and place of preparation;

2. Name and address of the legal mandator;

3. Name and address of the legal mandatory;

4. Full names and places of resident or working of individuals; full names and addresses or head
offices of agencies or organizations directly involved in legal mandate;

5. Contents of mutual legal assistance tasks in civil matters must specify the purpose of mutual
legal assistance, tasks and relevant circumstances, citation of applicable laws, measures to carry
out the mutual legal assistance and performance duration.

Article 13. Request for foreign legal assistance in civil matters

1. The competent authority of Vietnam, in the process of resolving civil matters, may request
foreign competent authority to provide legal assistance in the following cases:

a) Service of documents for the requested person who is in the foreign country;

b) Summon witnesses and experts residing in the requested countries

c) Collection and supply of evidence in the requested countries for settlement of civil matters in
Vietnam;

d) Other circumstances prescribed as per laws of Vietnam.

2. Requests for civil legal assistance by foreign countries shall be made in writing in the form of
civil legal mandate according to this Law.

Article 14. Procedures for requesting foreign countries to provide civil legal assistance

1. The competent authority of Vietnam shall prepare a written request for the overseas competent
authority to provide civil legal assistance in accordance with Article 11 of this Law and send it to
the Ministry of Justice.

2. Within 10 working days from the date on which a satisfactory request is received, the Ministry
of Justice shall record in the legal mandate book, verify the validity of the requests and send
them to foreign competent authority under the provisions of treaties to which Vietnam and those
foreign countries are members or through the diplomatic channel If the requests are
unsatisfactory, the Ministry of Justice shall return such requests to the request-making agencies
and provide an explanation therefore.

3. Within 05 working days after the receipt of foreign competent authorities' written notices on
the performance of legal mandate, the Ministry of Justice shall transfer the notices to Vietnam’s
competent authorities that have sent the civil legal mandate requests.

Article 15. Procedures for receiving and handling civil legal mandates of foreign countries

1. Within ten working days after the receipt of legal mandate requests of competent authorities of
the requesting countries, the Ministry of Justice shall record in the legal mandate book, verify the
validity of the requests and transfer them to competent authorities in Vietnam. If the requests are
unsatisfactory, the Ministry of Justice shall return such requests to the request-making agencies
and provide explanation therefor.

2. Within five working days after the receipt of written notices on the performance of legal
mandates from competent authorities in Vietnam, the Ministry of Justice shall transfer
the notices to competent authorities of the requesting countries in accordance with the treaties to
which Vietnam and the requesting countries are members or through the diplomatic channel.

3. If the legal mandate cannot be performed or the time limit has expired but the overseas
competent authority request supplementary documents, the competent authority in Vietnam shall
notify in writing the Ministry of Justice thereof and provide an explanation therefor. The
Ministry of Justice shall notify the overseas competent authority.

Article 16. Expenses for provision of civil legal assistance

1. Expenses for the provision of civil legal assistance between Vietnam and foreign countries
shall be paid by requesting countries, unless otherwise agreed upon.

2. Vietnamese individuals or organizations requesting competent authorities of Vietnam to
resolve civil cases that arise requiring for legal mandates overseas shall pay expenses according
to regulations of Vietnam and the requested countries. Within ten working days prior to the date
of deciding to make legal mandate request, the request-making agencies shall notify those
individuals or organizations of the expenses for performance of legal mandates. Legal mandate
requests shall be made and sent overseas only after those individuals or organizations pay the
expenses for performance of legal mandates according to regulations.

Vietnamese citizens entitled to legal assistance may be considered for support in expenses for
performance of legal mandates according to the Government’s regulations.

Chapter III

                     LEGAL ASSISTANCE IN CRIMINAL MATTERS

Article 17. Scope of criminal legal assistance

The scope of criminal legal assistance between Vietnam and foreign countries:

1. Service of papers, dossiers and documents related to criminal legal assistance;

2. Summon of witnesses and experts;

3. Collection and supply of evidence;

4. Criminal liability examination;

5. Information sharing;

6. Other requests for criminal legal assistance.

Article 18. Criminal legal assistance requests

1. The criminal legal assistance requests include:

a) A written request for criminal legal assistance from competent proceedings-
conducting authority.

b) The written criminal legal mandate as prescribed in Article 19 of this Law.

2. A criminal legal mandate request shall be made in sets in accordance with this Law and laws
of the requested country. Language used in the request complies with Article 5 of this Law.

Article 19. Letter of request for criminal legal assistance

1. A letter of request for criminal legal assistance includes:

a) Date, month, year and place of issuance;

b) Name and address of the legal mandator;

c) Name and address or head office of the legal mandatory;

d) Full names and places of permanent residence or working of individuals, full names,
addresses or head offices of agencies or organizations directly involved in the criminal legal
mandate;

dd) The tasks subject to criminal legal mandates, clearly indicating the mandate purpose;
summarized contents of the case, related circumstances, applicable legal provisions and
penalties; schedule of investigation, prosecution and trial; the mandate performance duration.

2. In addition to the contents defined in Clause 1 of this Article, depending on each specific case
and at the request of competent authorities of Vietnam or foreign countries, a letter of request for
criminal legal mandate may cover the following contents:

a) Signs of identity, nationality and places of residence of subjects in the criminal case or persons
having information relating to that case;

b) Matters to be questioned, questions to be asked, documents, requests or material evidences
shown and, if possible, a description of characters and appearance of persons requested to
present documents, requests and material evidences with regard to evidence collection mandates;

c) Contents of jobs, questions and requests for summoned witnesses and experts;

d) Description of assets and places where assets need to be searched for; grounds for determining
that the assets acquired from commission of crimes are located in the requesting country and
may fall under the jurisdiction of the requesting country; the execution of court judgments or
rulings on mandate for search, seizure of, or look for, confiscation of assets acquired from
commission of crimes;

dd) Measures applicable to the criminal legal mandate, which may lead to detection or recovery
of assets acquired from commission of crimes;

e) Requests or procedures of the requesting country to ensure the effective performance of legal
mandate, mode or form of supplying information, evidence, documents and articles;

g) Request for confidentiality of legal mandate;

h) Purpose, expected time and itinerary of the trip in case competent persons of the requesting
country need to arrive in the territory of the requested country for the purpose related to the legal
mandate;

i) The criminal judgment or ruling of a court and documents, evidence or other information
necessary for the performance of legal mandates.

3. In case the information stated in the letter of request for criminal legal mandate defined in
Clauses 1 and 2 of this Article is not sufficient for the performance of legal mandate, competent
authorities of the requested country may also send a written request for supplementary document
provision to the requesting country and fixing a specific deadline for reply.

Article 20. Requesting foreign countries to provide criminal legal assistance

1. Presiding authorities in Vietnam, in the course of criminal proceedings, may request overseas
competent authorities to provide legal assistance in the following cases:

a) Service of papers and documents on persons who are residing in the requested countries;

b/ Summon of witness and experts who are living in the requested countries;

c) Collection or supply of evidence in the requested countries for settlement of criminal cases in
Vietnam;

d) Examination of criminal liability of persons who are staying in the countries of which they
bear the nationality;

dd) Other cases prescribed by Vietnamese law.

2. Requests for criminal legal assistance from foreign countries must be made in the form of
criminal legal mandate under the provisions of this Law.

Article 21. Refusal or postponement of execution of criminal legal mandates of foreign
countries

1. A foreign criminal legal mandate shall be rejected in the following cases:

a) It does not conform to treaties to which Vietnam is a member or to Vietnamese law;

b) It causes harm to national sovereignty or security;

c) It is related to the criminal prosecution of a person for his/her criminal act for which he/she
was sentenced, declared unguilty or granted general or special amnesty in Vietnam;

d) It is related to criminal acts for which the statute of limitations of criminal prosecution has
expired under the provisions of Criminal Code of Vietnam;

dd) It is related to a violation against laws; however, do not constitute a crime under the
provisions of Criminal Code of Vietnam.

2. The execution of criminal legal mandates may be postponed in Vietnam if it obstructs the
process of investigation, prosecution, trial or judgment enforcement in Vietnam.

3. When deciding to refuse or postpone the execution of criminal legal mandates in accordance
with Clauses 1 and 2 of this Article, the Supreme People’s Procuracy shall send a notice to the
requesting countries, providing the explanation and measures to be applied.

Article 22. Procedures for criminal legal mandates to foreign countries

1. Presiding authorities in Vietnam requesting overseas competent authorities to provide criminal
legal assistance shall prepare a legal mandate requests as stipulated in Article 18 of this Law and
send them to the Supreme People’s Procuracy.

2. Within 10 working days from the date on which a satisfactory request is received, the
Supreme People’s Procuracy shall record in the legal mandate book, verify the validity of the
requests and send them to foreign competent authority under the provisions of treaties to which
Vietnam and those foreign countries are members or through the diplomatic channel. If the
requests are unsatisfactory, the Supreme People’s Procuracy shall return such requests to the
request-making agencies and provide explanation therefor.

3. Within 05 working days after the receipt of foreign competent authorities' written notices on
the execution of legal mandate, the Supreme People’s Procuracy shall transfer the notices to
Vietnam’s competent authorities that have sent the criminal legal mandate requests.

Article 23. Procedures for receiving and handling criminal legal mandates of foreign
countries

1. Within ten working days after the receipt of legal mandate requests of competent authorities of
the requesting countries, the Supreme People’s Procuracy shall record in the legal mandate
book, verify the validity of the requests and transfer them to competent authorities in Vietnam. If
the requests are unsatisfactory, the Supreme People’s Procuracy shall return such requests to the
request-making agencies and provide explanation therefor.

2. Within five working days after the receipt of written notices on the performance of legal
mandates from presiding authorities in Vietnam, the Supreme People’s Procuracy shall transfer
the notices to competent authorities of the requesting countries in accordance with the treaties to
which Vietnam and the requesting countries are members or through the diplomatic channel.

3. If the legal mandate cannot be performed or the time limit has expired but the overseas
competent authority request supplementary documents, the presiding authority in Vietnam shall
notify in writing the Supreme People’s Procuracy thereof and provide an explanation therefor.
The Supreme People’s Procuracy shall notify the overseas competent authority.

Article 24. Service of summons on witnesses, experts

1. The requesting countries wishing to summon witnesses or experts who are residing in Vietnam
shall send the summons to the Supreme People’s Procuracy at least ninety days before the
expected date of those persons presence in the requesting countries. The procedures to receive
summons of witnesses or experts comply with Article 23 of this Law.

2. Agencies serving the summons shall immediately send written certifications of such service to
the Supreme People’s Procuracy to forward them to the requesting countries; in case of non-
service, they shall notify such in writing and clearly state the reasons therefor.

Article 25. Transfer of persons who are serving their imprisonment sentence for supply of
evidence

1. Persons who are serving their imprisonment sentence in Vietnam may be transferred to
competent authorities of requesting countries for supply of evidence in criminal cases in the
requesting countries.

2. Competent authorities in Vietnam may transfer persons who are serving their imprisonment
sentence in accordance with Clause 1 this Article in the following cases:

a) Such persons agree with the transfer and to supply evidence in requesting countries;

b) Competent authorities of the requesting countries commit in writing to ensure their life safety
health, accommodation and meal, travel conditions, duration and mode of receipt and return as
well as other specific conditions related to the transfer as proposed by presiding authorities of
Vietnam. Such written commitment is made in accordance with the Vietnamese law and
international law related to the transfer of persons who are serving their imprisonment sentence
for supply of evidence. The return of transferees to presiding authorities of Vietnam must be
made on time as committed.

3. The duration for which the persons who are serving their imprisonment sentence are
transferred to and stay in the requesting countries is counted into their sentence-serving duration.

Article 26. Information provision

Upon request of competent authorities of Vietnam or foreign countries, the Supreme People’s
Procuracy shall request competent authorities of foreign countries or presiding authorities of
Vietnam to provide information relating to criminal legal assistance requests or copies of the
criminal judgments or decisions which have taken legal effect on citizens of the requesting
countries.

Article 27. Use of information and evidence in criminal legal assistance

1. Information or evidence provided by presiding authorities of Vietnam may be used only for
the purposes stated in the criminal legal mandates, must not be disclosed or transferred, unless
prior written consent of competent bodies of Vietnam is obtained.

2. Presiding authorities of Vietnam shall apply appropriate measures to keep secret criminal legal
mandates, mandate contents, enclosed documents and criminal proceedings to be conducted
under legal mandates. In case of non-performance of criminal legal mandates of foreign
countries under the law on protection of state secrets, the Supreme People’s Procuracy shall
notify in writing competent bodies of foreign countries thereof, clearly stating the
reasons therefor and reach agreement with the latter on substitute measures, if any.

3. When making criminal legal mandates to foreign countries, the Supreme People’s
Procuracy shall request competent authorities of such foreign countries to apply measures to:

a) Keep secret the information and evidence provided from Vietnam and use the information and
evidence within a scope necessary for the purpose stated in the criminal legal assistance request;

b) Ensure that information and evidence are not distorted, modified, illegally disclosed or
otherwise abused.

Article 28. Request for criminal prosecution; hand-over of files and material evidence of
cases to foreign countries

1. For cases involving foreigners who committed crimes in the Vietnamese territory but have
fled abroad and Vietnam has made an extradition request which was, however, rejected by
foreign competent authorities, the body which is handling the case shall transfer the case files to
the Supreme People’s Procuracy for requesting the countries where the offenders are present to
continue with the criminal prosecution. When deciding to transfer the case files, the Supreme
People’s Procuracy may also transfer material evidence of the cases.

2. The Supreme People’s Procuracy shall prescribe specific conditions for receipt and transfer of
case files and material evidence.

Article 29. Handling of foreign requests for criminal prosecution of Vietnamese citizens in
Vietnam

The Supreme People’s Procuracy shall consider requests of competent bodies of foreign
countries for further criminal prosecution of Vietnamese citizens who committed crimes
overseas and are present in Vietnam in the following order

1. If the case is being under investigation and falls under the jurisdiction of presiding authority of
a province or centrally affiliated cities (hereinafter referred to as “provincial-level presiding
authority"), such request will be transferred to the provincial-level People’s Procuracy of the
province where those Vietnamese citizens resided last before fleeing abroad in order to request
the investigating body of the same level to conduct the investigation; if the case falls under the
jurisdiction of the investigating body of the Ministry of Public Security, it will be transferred to
the investigating body of the Ministry of Public Security for investigation;

2. If the case is being under prosecution and falls under the jurisdiction of the provincial-level
People’s Procuracy, it will be transferred to the People’s Procuracy of the province where those
Vietnamese citizens last resided before fleeing abroad for prosecution;

3. The investigation, prosecution and trial applicable to the cases specified in this Article shall
comply with Vietnams criminal procedure laws.

Article 30. Execution of foreign legal mandates for investigation of foreign nationals in
Vietnam

Within five working days after the receipt of legal mandate requests for investigation of foreign
nationals, who have committed crimes in their countries and are residing in Vietnam, the
Supreme People’s Procuracy shall transfer the documents to investigating bodies of Vietnam for
investigation. Investigation results will be sent to the Supreme People’s Procuracy for transfer to
the requesting countries.

Article 31. Expenses for provision of criminal legal assistance

Expenses for the provision of criminal legal assistance between Vietnam and foreign countries
shall be paid by requesting countries, unless otherwise agreed upon. In case Vietnam bears the
cost of criminal legal mandate performance, such cost will be covered by the state budget.

Chapter IV

                                         EXTRADITION

Article 32. Extradition for criminal prosecution or execution of criminal judgments

1. Extradition means the hand-over by one country to another country of a person who has
committed a criminal act or been criminally sentenced and is being present in its territory so that
the extradition-requesting country to conduct the criminal prosecution or to execute the criminal
judgment.

2. Presiding authorities in Vietnam may:

a) Request competent authorities of foreign countries to extradite persons who have committed
criminal acts or been criminally sentenced and their sentences have already taken legal effect to
Vietnam for criminal prosecution or execution of criminal judgment;

b) Extradite foreigners residing in Vietnam, who have committed criminal acts or been
criminally sentenced and their sentences have already taken legal effect, to requesting countries
for criminal prosecution or execution of criminal judgment;

Article 33. Cases of extradition

1. Persons subject to extradition according to this Law are those who commit criminal acts for
which the Criminal Code of Vietnam and criminal laws of the requesting country prescribes
penalties of one or more years of imprisonment, life imprisonment or death penalty or who have
been sentenced to imprisonment by a court of the requesting country and the remaining
imprisonment duration is at least six months.

2. Criminal acts of the persons stipulated in Clause 1 of this Article are not required to be in the
same category of crimes or the same crime, and the factors that constitute their offenses are not
required to be the same under the laws of Vietnam and the requesting countries.

3. If the criminal acts of the persons stipulated in Clause 1 of this Article took place outside the
territory of the requesting countries, the extradition of offenders may be effected if those acts are
criminal acts prescribed in Criminal Code of Vietnam.

Article 34. Non-criminal prosecution, non-extradition to a third country

A person extradited to Vietnam shall not be subject to criminal prosecution or extradited to a
third country for acts committed abroad before their extradition to Vietnam, provided that such
acts do not constitute a crime in accordance with Criminal Code of Vietnam and are not included
in the extradition request of Vietnam or the third country.

In cases where Vietnam is requested to make extradition, the extradition shall only be carried out
if the requesting country commits not to prosecute for crimes other than those stated in the
extradition requests and not to extradite them to a third country, unless it is so agreed in writing
by Vietnam.

Article 35. Extradition refusal to foreign countries

1. Presiding authorities of Vietnam may refuse extradition of the extradition request falls under
one of the following cases:

a) The persons requested for extradition are Vietnamese citizens;

b) Pursuant to laws of Vietnam, the persons requested for extradition shall not be subject to
criminal prosecution or serve their penalties due to expired statute of limitations or other lawful
reasons;

c) The persons requested for extradition for criminal prosecution have already been condemned
by Vietnamese courts with legally effective judgments for the criminal acts stated in the
extradition requests or the cases have been suspended under Vietnams criminal procedure law;

d) The persons requested for extradition are those who are residing in Vietnam for reasons of
possible coercion in the extradition-requesting country due to discrimination of race, religion,
gender, nationality, ethnicity, social class or political viewpoint

dd) The extradition requests are related to different crimes and each crime can be examined for
penal liability under the law of the extradition-requesting country, but fail to comply with Clause
1, Article 33 of this Law.

2. Apart from the cases of extradition refusal specified in Clause 1 of this Article, presiding
authorities of Vietnam may refuse extradition of the extradition request falls under one of the
following cases:

a) Acts committed by persons requested for extradition are not crimes as per Criminal Code of
Vietnam;

b) Persons requested for extradition are subject to criminal prosecution in Vietnam for the
criminal acts stated in the extradition requests.

3. Presiding authorities of Vietnam that refuse extradition in accordance with Clauses 1 and 2
hereof shall notify competent authorities in the extradition-requesting countries thereof.

Article 36. Extradition requests

1. An extradition request must include:

a) A written extradition request of the competent authority;

b) Documents as prescribed in Article 37 of this Law.

2. The extradition request shall be made in three sets in accordance with this Law and the law of
the requesting country. Language used in the request complies with Article 5 of this Law.

Article 37. Written extradition requests and enclosed documents

1. A written extradition request must include:

a) Date, month, year and place of issuance;

b) Reason for the extradition request;

c) Name and address of the competent authority requesting the extradition;

d) Name and address of the authority requested to effect the extradition;

dd) Full name, gender, birth date, nationality, residence place of, and other necessary
information on, the person requested for extradition.

2. A written extradition request must be enclosed with the following documents:

a) Summarized content of the case;

b) Legal provisions applicable for the determination of factors constituting the crime and name
of the crime, the provisions on penalties, the statute of limitations for criminal prosecution or the
statute of limitations for enforcement of penalties against that crime;

c) Papers on the nationality and place of residence of the person requested for extradition, if any;

d) Other documents describing the identity and photos of the person requested for extradition as
required by international law and practice.

3. In case of requesting extradition for criminal prosecution, in addition to the documents
specified in Clauses 1 and 2 of this Article, the following documents are also required:

a) A copy of the arrest or detention warrant of a competent authority of the extradition-
requesting country;

b) A written certification that the person requested for extradition is the one mentioned in the
arrest or detention warrant.

4. In case of requesting extradition for judgment enforcement, in addition to the documents
specified in Clauses 1 and 2 of this Article, the following documents are also required:

a) A copy of the criminal judgment or decision of the court of the extradition-requesting country;

b) The written certification that the person requested for extradition is the one already sentenced.

Article 38. Receipt of extradition requests

Within 20 days from the date on which the extradition requests and enclosed documents are
received, the Ministry of Public Security shall record in the extradition dossier book and verify
them in accordance with Article 36 of this Law. The Ministry of Public Security may request the
competent authority of the extradition-requesting country to provide supplementary information.
After 60 days from the date on which the written request is sent, if the information is not
supplemented, the Ministry of Public Security shall return the requests to the requesting country
and provide an explanation. If the request is satisfactory, the Ministry of Public Security shall
forward it the competent regional People’s Court for consideration and decision.

Article 39. Consideration of extradition requests from multiple countries for one person

1. In the case where the Ministry of Public Security receives written requests from two or more
countries for the extradition of one person for the same crime or many different crimes, the
Ministry of Public Security shall take charge and cooperate with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs,
the Ministry of Justice, the Supreme People’s Procuracy and the Supreme People’s Court in
considering and deciding to execute the extradition request of one of the requesting countries and
transfer the extradition requests to the concerned regional People’s Court for extradition
consideration and decision.

2. Upon consideration of extradition requests prescribed in Clause 1 of this Article, in addition to
legal provisions, the following relevant factors must also be considered:

a) The effectual nationality and last place of residence of the person requested for extradition;

b) The legitimacy and compatibility of the extradition request;

c) Time and place of crime commission;

d) Specific interests of the requesting countries;

dd) The severity of the crime;

e) The nationality of the victim;

g) Possibility of subsequent extradition between the requesting countries;

h) Date of the extradition request;

i) Other relevant factors.

Article 40. Extradition decisions

1. Within 10 working days from the date of receiving the extradition request transferred by the
Ministry of Public Security, the regional People’s Court where the person requested for
extradition resides, is detained or held in custody or serves his/her imprisonment sentences shall
handle the request and notify the People’s Procuracy of the same level thereof in writing. During
the consideration of extradition requests, the regional People’s Court may request overseas
competent authorities to provide information to clarify the extradition requests. Written
extradition requests and written replies shall be sent via the Ministry of Public Security.

2. Within four months after handling the requests, the regional People’s Court shall, a case-by-
case basis, issue one of the following decisions:

a) Decision on consideration of extradition request when the conditions prescribed by this Law
are fully met;

b) Decision to suspend the consideration of the extradition request and return it to the Ministry of
Public Security in case the request does not fall under their jurisdiction or the foreign country
withdraws the extradition request or the person requested for extradition has left Vietnam or for
other reasons the consideration cannot proceed.

3. The regional People’s Court shall consider an extradition request within 30 days, from the date
on which the decision is issued in accordance with point a Clause 2 of this Article and send a set
of the request to the People’s Procuracy of the same level.

4. The extradition request shall be considered at sessions of a council consisting of three judges,
including a presiding judge, with the participation of members of the People’s Procuracy of the
same level.

The extradition request-considering council shall follow the order:

a) A council member presents the contents of the extradition requests and states his/her opinions
on the legal grounds of the extradition;

b) The procurator states the viewpoints of the People’s Procuracy;

c) The lawyer or lawful representative of the person requested for extradition presents his/her
opinions, if any;

d) The person requested for extradition states his/her opinions;

dd) Based on the provisions of this Law, relevant provisions of other Vietnamese laws and
treaties to which Vietnam is a member, the council discusses and decides by majority on the
extradition or extradition refusal.

5. Within 10 working days from the date on which the decision on extradition or extradition
refusal is issued, the regional People’s Court shall send such decision to the person requested for
extradition, the People’s Procuracy of the same level and the Ministry of Public Security for the
exercise of rights and performance of obligations according to law.

The person requested for extradition may appeal and the People’s Procuracy of the same level
may protest within fifteen days, the People’s Procuracy may protest within thirty days as from
the date the regional People’s Court issues decisions. The regional People’s Court shall forward
the requests, appeals and protests to the Supreme People’s Court within seven days from the date
the appeal or protest time limit expires.

Within 20 days after receiving the extradition requests and appeals or protests, the regional
People’s Court shall open a court session for appealed or protested decision consideration; the
appellate council shall decide on the extradition or extradition refusal. The order for examination
of appeals or protests against extradition decisions of regional People’s Courts shall comply with
Clause 4 of this Article.

6. Legally effective extradition decisions include:

a) Decisions of first-instance courts, which are not appealed or protested against;

b) Decisions of the courts of appeal.

Article 41. Precautionary measures for extradition

Upon receipt of official extradition requests of foreign countries, competent authorities of
Vietnam may apply precautionary measures under Vietnamese law and treaties to which
Vietnam is a member in order to ensure consideration of extradition requests.

Article 42. Enforcement of extradition decisions

1. Within 05 working days from the date on which the decision on extradition comes into force,
the Chief Justice of the regional People’s Court shall issue a decision on extradition enforcement.

Such decision shall be sent to the People’s Procuracies of the same level, the Ministry of Public
Security, the extradition-requesting countries and the extradited persons.

2. After the receipt of decision on extradition enforcement, the competent police office shall
proceed with the arrest of the extradited persons. The arrest of extradited persons shall comply
with laws on criminal procedures of Vietnam and treaties to which Vietnam is a member.

The Ministry of Public Security shall organize the extradition enforcement and send a notice to
the extradition-requesting countries thereof.

Article 43. Escorting the extradited person

1. The police office shall organize the escort of extradited persons according to the receipt time
and place agreed upon in advance in writing by Vietnam and the requesting country. The time
for receipt of an extradited person must not exceed fifteen days from the date on which the
decision on extradition enforcement comes into force.

2. If the time limit agreed upon in advance by concerned countries expires while the requesting
country fails to receive the extradited person, the Ministry of Public Security shall propose the
regional People’s Court that has issued the extradition decision to cancel the
enforcement decision and send a notice to the requesting country thereof.

Article 44. Postponement of extradition enforcement decisions and temporary extradition

1. In the case where the extradited person is subject to criminal prosecution or serving a sentence
within the territory of Vietnam for an offense other than the one requested for extradition, the
regional People’s Court that issued the decision for enforcement extradition may decide
postponing the extradition enforcement or postpone the extradition enforcement at the proposal
of the People’s Procuracies or police offices of the same level until the criminal prosecution
ends or the declared judgments are fully or partly served. The Ministry of Public Security shall
send a notice on postponement of extradition enforcement decisions to the requesting country at
least 10 working days prior to the expiration of the time limit for postponement of enforcement
of the extradition decisions. The Chief Judge of the regional People’s Court that has postponed
the enforcement of the extradition decision shall issue a decision for enforcement of extradition
decision and promptly send the decision enclosed with relevant documents to the competent
police office for notification to the requesting country and extradition enforcement as specific
agreement with the requesting country.

2. If the postponement of the enforcement of extradition decisions in accordance with Clause 1
of this Article obstructs the criminal prosecution process in the foreign country due to the
expiration of the statute of limitations therefor or causes serious difficulties for criminal
prosecution for the offense requested for extradition, at the proposal of the
People’s Procuracies or police offices and the proposal of the requesting countries, the
competent People's Court, based on Vietnamese law and a specific agreement with the
requesting country, may issue a temporary extradition decision in accordance with this Law.

3. The person under temporary extradition must be immediately returned to Vietnam after the
criminal proceedings of the requesting country have ended or the temporary extradition period
has expired as agreed upon by Vietnam and the foreign country. When there is a new extradition
request from the requesting country, in accordance with this Law, the People’s Court of Vietnam
shall consider agreeing on the new extradition if there are plausible reasons therefor.

Article 45. Re-extradition

In case the extradited person evades criminal prosecution or serving a sentence in a foreign
country and returns to Vietnam, the requesting country may request the re-extradition of that
person together with the documents as prescribed in Articles 36 and 37 of this Law; in this case,
the provincial-level Peoples Court shall not carry out the extradition decision procedure as
stipulated in Article 40 of this Law; the Chief Judge of the regional People’s Court that has
issued the extradition decision shall issue a re-extradition decision for such person. The escort of
re-extradited persons shall comply with Article 43 of this Law.

Article 46. Transfer of articles and material evidence related to criminal cases

Articles and material evidence acquired from crime commission or serving as proofs at court
sessions shall be considered transferring to the requesting country in accordance with treaties to
which Vietnam and the requesting country are members on the basis of respecting the rights of
the third party.

Article 47. Transit

1. On the basis of treaties to which Vietnam is a member and the provisions of Vietnamese laws,
the escort of extradited persons in transit through Vietnamese territory to the requesting country
shall be carried out only after being approved in writing by the competent authority of Vietnam
at the request of the foreign country.

2. In case of transfer by air and transit without landing in the territory of Vietnam, the application
for transit in Vietnam is not required. In case of landing, the extraditing country must
immediately send their requests for transit in accordance with Clause 1 of this Article.

Article 48. Extradition costs

The requesting country shall bear all costs related to extradition, unless otherwise agreed. In
cases where Vietnam bears the costs of extradition, the expenses shall be covered by the state
budget.

Chapter V

          TRANSFER OF PERSONS SERVING IMPRISONMENT SENTENCES

Article 49. Basis for transfer of persons serving imprisonment sentences

1. Persons serving imprisonment sentences may be transferred to the country of which they bear
the nationality or another country, which agree with the transfer for continued service of their
imprisonment sentences already declared against them by the transferring country.

2. The transfer shall be carried out based on treaties to which Vietnam is a member upon request
of the person serving imprisonment sentences or the competent authority of the

transferring country. In the case where there is not a treaty on transfer, the transfer of the person
serving imprisonment sentences shall be carried out under the direct agreement between
competent authorities of Vietnam and the concerned country in accordance with this Law, other
relevant laws of Vietnam, international laws and practice.

Article 50. Conditions for receipt and transfer of persons serving imprisonment sentences

1. A person serving imprisonment sentences overseas may be received back to Vietnam for
enforcement of imprisonment sentences when the following conditions are fully met:

a) He/she is a Vietnamese citizen;

b) He/she has the last place of residence in Vietnam;

c) The offense for which he/she was convicted abroad also constitutes a crime under Vietnamese
laws;

d) By the time of receiving the transfer requests, the remaining duration of serving the
imprisonment sentences must be at least one year; in special cases, this duration must be at least
six months;

dd) The judgment against the person to be transferred must be legally effective and there are no
pending legal proceedings against him/her in the transferring country;

e) The transfer has the consent of the transferring country;

g) The transfer has the consent of the person to be transferred.

2. A person serving imprisonment sentences in Vietnam may be transferred to a foreign country
for enforcement of imprisonment sentences when the following conditions are fully met:

a) He/she is citizen of the receiving country or is the person permitted to reside indefinitely or
having relatives in the receiving country;

b) He/she fully satisfies the conditions specified in points c, d, dd, e, and g Clause 1 of this
Article and has fulfilled his/her civil responsibilities and additional penalties such as fines,
property confiscation and other legal responsibilities in the judgments;

c) The transfer has the consent of the receiving country;

Article 51. Refusal to transfer persons serving imprisonment sentences

The competent authority of Vietnam shall refuse to transfer persons serving imprisonment
sentences in Vietnam to foreign countries in the following cases:

1. When they have grounds to believe that the person to be transferred may be tortured, retaliated
or oppressed in the receiving countries;

2. The transfer may harm the national sovereignty or security of Vietnam.

Article 52. Requests for transfer persons serving imprisonment sentences

1. A request for transfer of persons serving imprisonment sentences must include the following
documents:

a) A written request for transfer of a person serving imprisonment sentence issued by the
competent authority of the requesting country;

b) Enclosed documents specified in Article 53 of this Law.

2. The request for transfer persons serving imprisonment sentences must be prepared in three sets
in accordance with this Law and in compliance with the laws of the requesting country. The
language used to prepare the request must comply with Article 5 of this Law.

Article 53. Written request for transfer persons serving imprisonment sentences and
enclosed documents

1. A written request for transfer persons serving imprisonment sentences must include the
following contents:

a) Date, month, year, and place of preparation;

b) Reasons for requesting the transfer of the persons serving imprisonment sentences;

c) Name and address of the competent authority of the requesting country;

d) Name and address of the authority requested to transfer the persons serving imprisonment
sentences;

Full names, gender, date of birth, nationality and last residence place, the legal grounds proving
the legal status and other necessary information of the persons to be transferred.

2. Enclosed documents for transfer persons serving imprisonment sentences must include the
following documents and information:

a) Documents proving that the persons to be transferred meet the conditions specified in Article
50 of this Law;

b) Written summary of the contents of the case, copies of the court judgments or decisions
against the persons serving imprisonment sentences;

c) Applicable laws to determine constituent elements of a crime and crime, penalties, statute of
limitations for judgment enforcement;

d) Written description of the identity characters and photos of the person requested for transfer as
provided for by international law and practice;

dd) Documents and materials certifying the duration for which the person requested for transfer
has served his/her imprisonment sentences in the country requested for transfer and the
remaining duration for which he/she shall serve his/her imprisonment sentences in the receiving
country;

e) Documents related to the health conditions, mental status, medical records of the person
requested for transfer (if any);

g) The treaty between the requested country and the receiving country.

Article 54. Receipt of requests for transfer of persons serving imprisonment sentences

Within twenty days from the date on which the request for transfer of persons serving
imprisonment sentences and enclosed documents are received, the Ministry of Public Security
shall record in the transfer dossier book and verify the request as prescribed in Articles 52 and 53
of this Law. The Ministry of Public Security shall request the competent authorities of the
requesting country to provide supplementary information. If the supplementary information is
not provided within sixty days from the date of sending the request for supplementary
information, the Ministry of Public Security shall return the request for transfer of persons
serving imprisonment sentences and provide an explanation to the requesting country. If the
request is satisfactory, the Ministry of Public Security shall forward 02 sets of the request to the
competent regional People’s Court for consideration and decision.

Article 55. Decision on transfer of persons serving their imprisonment sentences in
Vietnam to foreign countries

1. Within ten working days from the receipt of satisfactory request for transfer of persons serving
their imprisonment sentences in Vietnam to foreign countries from the Ministry of Public
Security, the People’s Court of the province where the person serving his/her imprisonment
sentence shall handle the case and send a notice to the provincial-level People’s Procuracy
thereof. During the consideration of the request, the provincial-level People’s Court may request
competent authorities of the foreign country to provide information to clarify such request.
Written requests and written replies shall be sent via the Ministry of Public Security.

2. Within thirty days after handling the requests, the regional People’s Court shall, on a case-by-
case basis, issue one of the following decisions:

a) Decision on consideration of transfer request when the conditions prescribed in Article 50 this
Law are fully met;

b) Decision to suspend the consideration of the transfer request and return it to the Ministry of
Public Security in case the request does not fall under their jurisdiction or the competent
authority of foreign country withdraws the transfer request or the person requested for transfer
has left Vietnam or for other reasons that the consideration cannot proceed.

3. Within 30 days from the date on which the decision is issued in accordance with point a
Clause 2 of this Article, the regional People’s Court shall consider the transfer request and
forward a set of the request to the People’s Procuracy of the same level.

4. The transfer request shall be considered at the session of a council consisting of three judges,
including a presiding judge, with the participation of members of the People’s Procuracy of the
same level.

The transfer request-considering council shall follow the order:

a) A council member presents the contents of the transfer requests and states his/her opinions on
the legal grounds of the transfer;

b) The procurator states the viewpoints of the People’s Procuracy;

c) The lawyer or lawful representative of the person requested for transfer presents his/her
opinions, if any;

d) The person requested for transfer states his/her opinions;

dd) Based on the provisions of this Law, relevant provisions of other Vietnamese laws and
treaties to which Vietnam is a member, the council discusses and decides by majority on the
transfer or transfer refusal.

5. Within 10 working days from the date on which the decision on transfer or transfer refusal is
issued, the regional People’s Court shall send such decision to the person requested for transfer,
the People’s Procuracy of the same level and the Ministry of Public Security for the exercise of
rights and performance of obligations according to law.

The person requested for transfer may appeal and the People’s Procuracy of the same level may
protest within fifteen days, the People’s Procuracy may protest within thirty days as from the
date the regional People’s Court issues decisions. The regional People’s Court shall forward the
requests, appeals and protests to the Supreme People’s Court within seven days from the date the
appeal or protest time limit expires.

Within 20 days after receiving the transfer requests and appeals or protests, the regional
People’s Court shall open a court session for appealed or protested decision consideration; the
appellate council shall decide on the transfer or transfer refusal. The order for examination of
appeals or protests against transfer decisions of regional People’s Courts shall comply with
Clause 4 of this Article.

6. Legally effective transfer decisions include:

a) Decisions of first-instance courts, which are not appealed or protested against;

b) Decisions of the courts of appeal.

Article 56. Authority to decide receiving persons serving their imprisonment sentences in
foreign countries back to Vietnam

The regional People’s Court where the person to be transferred last resides in Vietnam shall
decide the receipt. The procedures for receipt consideration shall comply with Article 55 of this
Law.

Article 57. Enforcement of decisions for transfer of persons serving imprisonment
sentences

1. Within five working days from the date on which the People’s Court’s decision for transfer of
a person serving imprisonment sentence comes into force, the Chief Justice of the People's Court
that has issued the first-instance decision shall issue the decision for enforcement of transfer
decisions. The decision on enforcement of transfer decisions shall be sent to the provincial-level
People’s Procuracy, the Ministry of Public Security, the competent authority of the requesting
country and the person requested for transfer.

2. The Ministry of Public Security shall organize the transfer specified in Clause 1 of this Article
and send a notice to the requesting country thereof.

Article 58. Continuing to serve the sentences in Vietnam

1. The continuation of serving the imprisonment sentence in Vietnam for the transferee shall
comply with the laws of Vietnam.

2. In the cases where the length of time of the foreign penalty corresponds with the laws of
Vietnam, the competent People's Court shall issue a decision to accept the transfer. The decision
to accept the transfer must clearly state the length of time for which the transferee must continue
to serve the imprisonment sentence in Vietnam.

If the nature or the length of time of the sentence imposed by the transferring country does not
correspond with the laws of Vietnam, the competent People's Court shall make a decision to
accept the transfer based on the circumstances of the case and convert the sentence to comply
with the Criminal Code of Vietnam. The length of time for which the transferee must continue to
serve the imprisonment sentence in Vietnam shall not exceed the sentence imposed in the
transferring country.

3. Upon receiving notification of special amnesty, general amnesty, penalty exemption or
reduction decisions of the transferring countries for the person serving imprisonment sentence,
the Ministry of Public Security shall immediately send such notices to competent authorities for
consideration and decision.

Article 59. Escort of transferees

1. The Ministry of Public Security shall organize the escort of persons serving
imprisonment sentence to the place and at the time agreed upon in writing by competent
authorities of Vietnam and the requesting country.

2. If the agreed time limit provided for in Clause 1 of this Article has expired while the
requesting country refuse to receive the transferee, the Ministry of Public Security shall propose
the competent People’s Court that has issued the transfer decision to cancel the decision on
enforcement of the transfer decision and notify the requesting country thereof.

Article 60. Costs for transfer of persons serving imprisonment sentences

The country requesting the transfer of a person serving imprisonment sentence shall bear all
expenses for the transfer, unless otherwise agreed. In cases where Vietnam bears the costs of
transferring a person serving imprisonment sentence, the expenses shall be covered by the state
budget.

Chapter VI

    RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGULATORY AGENCIES IN LEGAL ASSISTANCE
                             ACTIVITIES

Article 61. Responsibilities of the Government of Vietnam in legal assistance activities

1. Perform the unified state management of legal assistance activities

2. Direct Governmental agencies in legal assistance activities; cooperate with the Supreme
People’s Court and the Supreme People’s Procuracy in legal assistance activities.

3. Annually report to the National Assembly of Vietnam on legal assistance activities.

Article 62. Responsibilities of the Ministry of Justice

1. Assist the Government in performing the unified state management of legal assistance
activities

2. Receive, transfer, monitor and urge the implementation of civil legal mandates.

3. Exchange information on legal assistance laws and practice of legal assistance with
competent authorities of foreign countries under the provisions of treaties to which Vietnam is a
member.

 4. Propose the conclusion of, accession to, and enforcement of, international treaties on legal
assistance; Propose amendments and supplements to, and improvement of laws on legal
assistance of Vietnam.

5. Annually report to the Government of Vietnam on legal assistance activities.

Article 63. Responsibilities of the Supreme People's Court

1. Guide the People’s Courts at all levels to provide legal assistance.

2. (annulled)

3. Biannually and annually notify the Ministry of Justice of the provision of legal assistance
under its jurisdiction.

Article 64. Responsibilities of the Supreme People’s Procuracy

1. Receive, transfer, monitor and urge the performance of criminal legal mandates;
consider deciding on the performance of, and request the competent Peoples Procuracies or
investigating authorities to perform criminal legal mandates; refuse or postpone the performance
of criminal legal mandates according to its competence.

2. Perform the prosecution and control legal assistance activities according to its competence.

3. Guide the People’s Procuracies at all levels to provide criminal legal assistance.

4. Propose the conclusion of, accession to, and enforcement of, international treaties on legal
assistance; propose amendments and supplements to, and improvement of laws on legal
assistance of Vietnam.

5. Biannually and annually notify the Ministry of Justice of the provision of criminal legal
mandates.

Article 65. Responsibilities of the Ministry of Public Security

1. Receive, transfer, consider and settle foreign countries requests for extradition and transfer of
persons serving the imprisonment sentences; consider and transfer requests to
People’s Procuracies, People’s Courts; and conduct legal assistance activities according to its
competence.

2. Propose the conclusion of, accession to, and implementation of, treaties on extradition and
transfer of persons serving the imprisonment sentences; propose amendments and supplements
to, and improvement of laws on legal assistance of Vietnam.

3. Biannually and annually notify the Ministry of Justice of the implementation of requests for
extradition and transfer of persons serving the imprisonment sentences.

Article 66. Responsibilities of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs

1. Take lead and cooperate with relevant ministries and departments in consideration and
decision on the application of the reciprocity principle in legal assistance relations with relevant
countries.

2. Propose the conclusion of, accession to, and enforcement of, international treaties on legal
assistance; propose amendments and supplements to, and improvement of laws on legal
assistance of Vietnam.

3. Biannually and annually notify the Ministry of Justice of the application of reciprocity in legal
assistance relations with relevant countries.

Article 67. Responsibilities of overseas representative commissions of Vietnam

1. Perform legal mandates related to Vietnamese nationals in host countries at the request of
competent regulatory agencies in accordance with laws of Vietnam, treaties to which Vietnam is
a member and not contrary to the laws of host countries.

2. Receive legal mandate requests of foreign countries and transfer them to competent authorities
in Vietnam.

3. Transfer legal mandate requests of competent authorities of Vietnam to the Ministry of
Foreign Affairs of the host country for further transfer to competent authorities of those countries
for consideration and implementation.

Article 68. Responsibilities of regional People’s Court and provincial-level People’s Courts

1. Responsibilities of regional People’s Courts:

a) Perform legal mandates of foreign countries as per this Law.

b) Consider deciding on the extradition and transfer of persons serving imprisonment sentences
or refuse the extradition and transfer of persons serving imprisonment sentences as per this Law;

c) Conduct other legal assistance activities according to their competence;

d) Report on the provision of legal assistance to the provincial-level People's Courts for
consolidation and notification to the Supreme People’s Court.

2. Responsibilities of provincial-level People’s Courts:

a) Consider appeals or protests against decisions on extradition or transfer of persons serving
imprisonment sentences under jurisdiction;

b) Report on the results of provision of legal assistance to the Supreme People’s Court.

Article 69. Responsibilities of the provincial-level People’s Procuracy

1. Perform legal mandates of foreign countries under this Law.

2. Conduct other legal assistance activities according to their competence.

3. Perform the prosecution and control legal assistance activities according to its competence.

4. Report on the results of provision of legal assistance to the Supreme People’s Procuracy.

Article 70. Responsibilities of investigating authority

1. Receive requests for legal assistance in criminal matters, extradition, and transfer of persons
serving imprisonment sentences from competent authorities.

2. Conduct legal assistance activities in criminal matters, extradition, and transfer of persons
serving imprisonment sentences as per this Law and other relevant regulations.

3. Report on the results of providing legal assistance in criminal matters, extradition, and transfer
of persons serving imprisonment sentences to competent authorities.

Chapter VII

                                            IMPLEMENTATION CLAUSES

Article 71. Effect

This Law shall come into force from July 01, 2008.

Article 72. Implementation

The Government of Vietnam and the Supreme People’s Procuracy shall elaborate and guide the
implementation of this Law./.

                                                                                CHAIRPERSON

                                                                                 Le Quang Tung

                                                       LUẬT

                                             TƯƠNG TRỢ TƯ PHÁP

  Luật Tương trợ tư pháp số 08/2007/QH12 ngày 21 tháng 11 năm 2007 của Quốc hội, có hiệu lực kể từ ngày 01
